sections.html:
Eighteen miles from downtown Salt Lake, South Jordan fills the south-central Salt Lake Valley across roughly 22 square miles. Ground rises from the Jordan River at about 4,300 feet to the Oquirrh foothills near 5,200 feet. Population hit 77,487 in the 2020 Census, a jump from 50,418 in 2010, and 2020 to 2024 estimates put median home value at $650,500 with 81.4% of homes owner-occupied.

Treat that median as a survey figure and not as your price. A house wanting a roof, a basement finish or a kitchen update lands below it, and a lakeview Daybreak home can land above. Newer construction means buyers tend to quiz sellers about roof age and whether finished basements were permitted.

One county covers the whole city, so valuation, billing and deeds all run through Salt Lake County's Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder, and Jordan School District serves every address.

The big change came in 2004, when Kennecott Land started Daybreak, a master-planned community of about 4,200 acres on the west side. The 1,300 undeveloped acres that remained were sold to Larry H. Miller Group in 2022, and a new Downtown Daybreak opened in 2025 with the Salt Lake Bees ballpark as its anchor.

The city's FAQ places Downtown Daybreak in a Housing Transit Reinvestment Zone along the Mountain View Corridor, between two existing TRAX stations, and expects it to add housing and transit use in the fastest-growing quadrant of the county. If you live on the west side, plan for more construction nearby for several more years, with the noise, traffic and showing-schedule effects that come with it.

Getting around is a strength, and it is what buyers raise first. Interstate 15 skirts the eastern boundary, exiting at 10600 South and 11400 South, while Bangerter Highway cuts through the center with interchanges at 9800, 10400 and 11400 South.

  • TRAX Red Line: three stations in Daybreak, at South Jordan Parkway, South Jordan Downtown and Daybreak Parkway. The ride from Daybreak Parkway to downtown Salt Lake City takes about 60 minutes.
  • FrontRunner commuter rail: a station at 10200 South.
  • Public schools: Jordan School District, including Bingham High and Herriman High.
  • Charter and private options: Paradigm High, Early Light Academy, Hawthorne Academy, American Heritage and Stillwater Academy.

Owners may run short-term rentals in condos, townhouses, single-family houses and guest houses. A guest house needs an approved accessory dwelling unit permit. Internal ADUs such as basement apartments cannot be used as short-term rentals.

A basement that was once listed on Airbnb can draw questions from a lender or inspector, and the unit may count as long-term rental space only. Under city code 5.04.100 a business license cannot be transferred, and applications go through the city's online portal. Whoever buys starts fresh, which is why any rental income you mention needs careful wording.

Both are common along the Wasatch Front, and both tend to surface during inspection. The Wasatch Fault is about 240 miles long, and experts put the odds of a magnitude 6.0 or larger earthquake within 50 years at 57%. Magna felt a magnitude 5.7 shake in March 2020, and the valley saw moderate damage.

On radon, the state program estimates one in three Utah homes runs high and sets 4 picocuries per liter as the action level. It recommends testing, with mitigation above that number, so a high reading could put a mitigation system on the repair list. With cash and an as-is deal, such items become a line in the price talk instead of a dispute after inspection.

Salt Lake County sends the bill. Because Utah exempts 45% of a primary residence's value, 55% of market value is what gets taxed.

Pay late and the penalty is the greater of 2.5% or $10, though 1% applies when everything is settled by January 31. If you sell during the year, the title company prorates the bill, so ask it for the figure before you sign.

Reach the Treasurer at 2001 S State St, Suite N1-200, Salt Lake City, (385) 468-8300, for the balance due on a parcel. The Recorder handles your deed from Suite N1-600, (385) 468-8145. Phone the Recorder to check whether a deed or lien has been filed against the property.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in South Jordan
sections.html:
Without a lender in the picture, nobody sits through appraisal or underwriting. Ask for an offer, let the buyer look over the house and run the figures, then pick the closing date that matches your move.

Closing still goes through a title or escrow company, which records the deed with the county. Taxes are split by days of ownership. Pull together paperwork on the roof, the HVAC system and any basement finish before asking for offers, because a serious buyer will want to read it. At the table, bring photo ID, payoff details for any loan, and every key and opener.

A listing can bring a higher price when the house shows well and you are not in a hurry. It also means showings, an inspection, buyer repair requests and a lender's appraisal, any of which can slow or break a deal. Cash trades some of that price for speed and certainty. Request an offer, weigh it against what a listing would net after fees and repairs, and decide. You owe nothing for asking.

If you owe back taxes, the balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, so tell the title company early and it can get the payoff figure from the Treasurer.

sections.h2: Common snags for South Jordan sellers
sections.html:
• Basement or garage conversions done without a permit, which the city will not count as legal units.
  • Past short-term renting that breaks the city's rules for that kind of property.
  • Daybreak construction nearby that affects noise, traffic and showings.
  • High radon results that surface late in a financed sale.
  • A tight timeline when you have already bought another house.

Spot any of these before the first showing, and each is far easier to deal with.

faqs.q: Is South Jordan in Salt Lake County?
faqs.a: Yes. South Jordan sits entirely in Salt Lake County, so the county Assessor, Treasurer and Recorder handle your valuation, tax bill and deed. Jordan School District serves the city.

faqs.q: When are South Jordan property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30 is the last day to pay without a penalty. Taxes unpaid on December 1 become delinquent, with a late fee that drops to 1% if you pay by January 31.

faqs.q: Can I use a basement apartment in South Jordan as an Airbnb?
faqs.a: No. Internal ADUs such as basement apartments cannot be short-term rentals. Condos, townhouses, single-family houses and permitted guest houses can be, subject to the city's license rules.

faqs.q: How many people live in South Jordan?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 77,487 people, up from 50,418 in 2010. Estimates for 2020 to 2024 show about 26,740 households and an owner-occupied rate of 81.4%.

faqs.q: Can I sell a South Jordan house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as is to a cash buyer, who prices in repairs such as an old roof or a bad basement finish. Ask for the offer in writing and compare it with what you would net after repairs and listing costs.
